{"local_delta": -0.03,
  "departures": [
    {"fact": "In England the post-April-2025 equality settlement operates as concrete day-to-day guidance: the EHRC code of practice (20 May 2025) tells service providers and businesses they may demand a birth certificate where there is 'genuine concern' about biological sex, and that trans people may be excluded from single-sex sport 'when necessary'. This is the operative rule a trans visitor meets at venues, transport, spas, gyms and services, and it converts a document mismatch into a forced outing and possible ejection.",
     "local_evidence": "News reporting (20 May 2025): the national equality body 'updated its code of practice after the 2025 ruling, advising that services and businesses may ask for a person's birth certificate where there is genuine concern about biological sex, and that trans people may be excluded from single-sex sport when necessary for safety. This is the operative enforcement guidance a trans visitor meets at venues, transport and services day to day.'",
     "direction": "riskier",
     "magnitude": 0.03,
     "visitor_applicability": "Reaches visitors directly: hotels, venues, sports facilities and transport operators may check documents or exclude on biological-sex grounds, outing the traveller and denying service. Not a resident-only regime.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": true},
    {"fact": "Prison and police-custody allocation in England follows biological sex, with Article 8 conferring no automatic right to accommodation with the opposite biological sex; the 19 June 2026 judgment applied the April 2025 definition ruling to custody.",
     "local_evidence": "Local bundle: 'Prison and custody decisions in England are governed by the same national ruling' and the 19 June 2026 judgment 'confirms the biological-sex custody logic that the same ruling imposes on this state/province's prison and custody decisions'.",
     "direction": "riskier",
     "magnitude": 0.02,
     "visitor_applicability": "Only reaches a visitor if arrested or detained; a real but low-frequency exposure for a short-stay traveller, and the same biological-sex logic is already national.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": true,
     "counted_in_delta": false},
    {"fact": "Official hate-crime baseline for England and Wales: 115,990 police-recorded hate crimes in the year ending March 2025, transgender strand down 11% year on year, against a survey estimate of ~176,000 incidents.",
     "local_evidence": "Official statistics (9 Oct 2025), with the bulletin's own caution that recorded figures understate prevalence and that a February 2024 capital-city recording change breaks comparison.",
     "direction": "safer",
     "magnitude": 0.0,
     "visitor_applicability": "Aggregate resident-reported crime data; raw counts with no population denominator and only a percentage change for the trans strand, so it cannot be read as a per-capita rate or as a trans-specific visitor exposure.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": false},
    {"fact": "Regional LGBTI comparative scoring (1st in 2015 at 86%, 22nd in 2025 at 45%) and general LGB acceptance polling.",
     "local_evidence": "Secondary factors: the organisation's 'comparative scoring places the parent nation first in the region in 2015... 22nd in 2025 with 45%', expressly parent-nation-wide rather than England-specific; no trans-specific acceptance polling exists.",
     "direction": "riskier",
     "magnitude": 0.0,
     "visitor_applicability": "Parent-wide climate signal only, and LGB-wide rather than trans-specific; not a local departure and not a countable visitor exposure.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": true,
     "counted_in_delta": false}
  ],
  "inherited_national_exposure": [
    "GRA 2005 era framework and the non-recognition of 50 foreign GRC regimes since December 2023 — national, untouched by local evidence.",
    "National transport police strip-search policy amended April 2025 to search trans women by sex at birth — national, do not re-count.",
    "National single-sex-spaces guidance in force August 2026 and UN experts' warning of 18 August 2026 on equality-act revisions — national.",
    "NHS ward-exclusion plans, puberty-blocker ban and Joelle's death / clinical-negligence claim — national health exposure, do not re-count.",
    "Hostile national media climate, falling rainbow-index ranking, school and rugby exclusions — national climate signals.",
    "The UKSC April 2025 'woman = biological sex' ruling and the 19 June 2026 custody judgment are named in the national dossier; only their England-specific operative implementation is treated as a local item."
  ],
  "uncertainty": "The England bundle is largely a restatement of the national framework ('England stands under the parent nation's national framework, which the national record carries'), so most items are inherited and count for nothing. The only genuine local departure is the EHRC code's operative birth-certificate and single-sex-sport provisions, and whether that code's 'genuine concern' standard is tested or applied in practice is explicitly unsourced; the unresolved 5 February 2026 judicial review and the unretrievable force searching policy are open questions, not exposures, and were given no weight.",
  "notes": "Delta is small and negative. England adds one documented traveller-facing implementation — the equality-body code permitting birth-certificate demands on 'genuine concern' and exclusions from single-sex sport — a conditional but universal-style exposure at venues, transport and services that the national bundle does not itemise for this division. Custody-by-biological-sex is genuinely present but duplicates the national record, so it is not re-counted; hate-crime counts lack denominators and the rainbow-index scoring is parent-wide and LGB-wide, so neither moves the delta. No local protective machinery operating for trans visitors is documented, so nothing offsets."
}
